findings.title: Bitcoin/Ethereum provider response ceiling is checked after unbounded body buffering
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Reviewer recommends fixing before publishing the affected connected tools; the intended availability ceiling is not enforced during ingestion. This does not demonstrate secret compromise or affect the offline tools.
findings.affectedBuilds: Multi-Chain Activity Viewer and Discovery Scanner Bitcoin/Ethereum HTTP paths. Dash's separate streamed reader, offline Deriver and Inspector are outside the demonstrated defect.
findings.reproduction: Run pnpm exec vitest run --config docs/audits/AUD-021-harnesses/vitest.config.mjs. The first test supplies production fetchJson a finite 22 x 1 MiB synthetic ReadableStream through a stubbed fetch. The second applies the existing Dash streamed JSON reader to the same fixture and ceiling. No real provider or wallet is contacted.
findings.expected: Cancel body ingestion once actual received bytes exceed the configured maximum; do not require buffering the entire untrusted body before rejecting it.
findings.observed: Public provider emitted all 22 chunks and was not cancelled: {emitted:22,cancelled:false}. Only then did the size-limit error fire. The safety assertion failed; the Dash bounded-reader control passed. Current text.length counts UTF-16 code units, not received bytes.
findings.impact: An unexpectedly large or hostile response from an approved external provider can cause excessive allocation, Worker/page unresponsiveness or memory exhaustion before rejection. The finite probe demonstrates ineffective ingestion limiting, not an actual OOM, key leak or unauthorized transaction. Exploitation requires an oversized provider response; arbitrary endpoint injection is not demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Read the Response stream under a named byte ceiling and cancel its reader as soon as limit+1 is observed. Content-Length may be an early check but cannot be authoritative. Reuse the existing bounded-reader pattern through a neutral shared layer without a module cycle; preserve timeout/abort through body decoding and fail closed on malformed JSON.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain this failing production-path test and make it pass after the fix. Add exact-limit and limit+1 byte cases, absent/false Content-Length, multi-byte UTF-8 and body-phase abort. Verify provider/controller failures remain error or incomplete rather than zero-balance success. Rerun nearest provider/adapter tests and affected browser cases.

findings.title: Six displayed release passports retain the previous wasm-bindgen version
findings.affectedBuilds: Activity Viewer, Discovery Scanner and Key Derivation Tool in both editions.
findings.reproduction: Build the current eight HTML pages and run python3 docs/audits/AUD-021-harnesses/check-metadata.py. Compare the rendered release-passport wasm-bindgen phrase with packages/dash-shielded-wasm/rust/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, and the canonical Docker pin.
findings.expected: Displayed dependency metadata agrees with the exact 0.2.129 WASM library/CLI version used for the freshly verified local integrations.
findings.observed: All six applicable HTML passports display wasm-bindgen 0.2.128; canonical Cargo inputs and Docker builder use 0.2.129. Six mismatches reproduced. The separate upstream MHFE package's own internal versions are not the source of this phrase.
findings.impact: Incorrect source/build information misleads a reviewer about the shipped runtime. Binary integrity and deterministic outputs still passed; no cryptographic or spending defect is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the three template passages to the current version and preferably derive this displayed field from the same canonical metadata source so future upgrades do not leave it stale.
findings.requiredVerification: Rebuild both editions and make the six passport comparisons pass; verify source/provenance/CSP hashes and artifact gates after the template edit. Do not rewrite unrelated upstream MHFE notices.

limitations: Full scope was reviewed, but this is a recorded engineering audit, not independent cryptographic certification or proof that all defects are absent.
No real private material, live mainnet/testnet provider scan, Core regtest, hardware-wallet interoperability, real publication or publisher-signature validation was performed.
Only 70 of 35,156 legal build combinations were compiled; representative selective variants were runtime-tested. Dedicated assistive-technology acceptance was not performed.

MHFE's full-cost 2 GiB vector corpus, threaded execution and suite 4 were not exercised here. The embedded upstream MHFE 0.4.0 package documents suite 3; its reduced-cost fixed vector and UI Worker boundaries passed.

The four local WASM modules were rebuilt; the separate hash-pinned MHFE browser package was not regenerated. Neither all upstream dependency internals nor alternative operating systems were manually audited.
RustSec has unmaintained atomic-polyfill and paste warnings despite zero vulnerability advisories. Advisory absence is not a correctness guarantee.
GitHub returned no runs for the reviewed commit. Local checks and static workflow review do not establish remote CI/release completion.

The Docker suite skipped one optional Poppler assertion and ignored one intentional Rust fixture-regeneration helper. The Poppler assertion subsequently passed on the host; skipped filtered tests were not counted as new passes.

Native build:html updated eight tool pages, not earlier dist release folders. Only fresh canonical release bundles and the identified eight browser-tested native pages are approved by the build checks.
No product source changed. Retained additions are this report pair, audit index entry and reproducible harnesses; generated evidence remains ignored and local.
